title: Kvarta: white + warm accents
question: Three new layouts using your white background, bright warm accents and typography reference. Compare the composition and ordering experience; the business facts are the same.

options.label: A note from Kvarta
options.thesis: A direct invitation from the workshop, with the offer and callback slip in one clear white composition.
options.viewport: An asymmetric typographic dispatch note puts the real offer and request fields first; the Thursday/Friday schedule supports it.
options.risk: The typography needs enough character and breathing room to avoid looking like a plain form.

options.label: One fresh pack
options.thesis: A single white coffee pack with a vivid orange label gives the offer a tangible focal point.
options.viewport: One product artifact anchors a vertical white page; prices and a labelled callback slip sit in the same reading path, without a copy/photo split.
options.risk: Strong packaging photography is essential, and the product must not push the action too far down.

options.label: Thursday → Friday
options.thesis: Two bold day markers make the freshness promise the structure of the opening.
options.viewport: A short chronological sequence leads directly into the real offers and callback form; the first catalog entry begins below.
options.risk: The day typography must remain warm and simple rather than turning the page into an infographic.
